n239d0ecbe3e4: Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease1. Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model2,3. Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor—encapsulated within a GalNAc–lipid nanoparticle—leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

n1fec017c1693: Basophils are rare cells best known for their role in allergy but their contribution to cancer remains poorly understood. n3d301d4bd652: β-thalassemia is an extensively studied monogenic disorder, yet the basis of its striking phenotypic diversity remains unresolved. Here we present the 1000 β-Thalassemia Genomes Project (KbTGP), providing the first comprehensive atlas of 1,429 Chinese genomes (1,020 probands and 409 unaffected parents, 61.63× coverage) linked to 77 clinical traits. We identify 11 independent phenotype-associated loci in probands, and 15 additional loci by integrating 2,746 ethnically matched controls from the NyuWa Project and the 1000 Genomes Project. Functional experiments further highlight non-coding regions at 17p13.3 and the autophagy-related gene PIK3C3 as modulators of thalassemic phenotypes. These findings collectively establish a phenome-genome resource that delineates the genetic architecture of β-thalassemia, offering candidate targets for precision therapies and laying the groundwork for future research into dissecting the Mendelian disease variability. n21e738e70a75: Although highly preventable, cervical cancer remains one of the most common malignancies among women worldwide. As part of the Global Burden of Disease study, we estimated cervical cancer incidence, mortality and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. In 2023, 887,000 new cases (95% uncertainty interval 682,000–1,170,000), 369,000 deaths (292,000–475,000) and 13.3 million DALYs (10.1–17.4) were estimated globally. Age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) were more than four and seven times higher in low- versus high-income countries. Between 1990 and 2023, global ASIR was largely stable (−0.4% (–26.6 to 34.7)), whereas ASMR changed by −17.5% (–36.2 to 13.4). All cervical cancer DALYs were attributable to human papillomavirus infection, with tobacco use contributing 5.9% (3.2–9.3) globally. By 2050, global ASIR and ASMR are forecast to change by −12.5% (–25.7 to 3.5) and −9.0% (–21.5 to 6.6) from 2024, yet absolute cases and deaths are forecast to rise by 20.2% (4.6–38.5) and 39.3% (23.6–57.3). na4ef69ba7a30: There is an unmet need for repigmentation therapies for patients with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV) who are candidates for systemic therapy. n453fd2048dc4: During translation, transfer RNAs (tRNAs) deliver specific amino acids to the ribosome in a coordinated manner with the sequence encoded by the messenger RNA. Altogether, tRIBO-seq offers a robust and reproducible approach to map the full tRNA landscape—capturing tRNA abundance, modification and fragmentation patterns—across both total and actively translating tRNA populations, revealing the dynamics of the tRNAome with unprecedented resolution, in a single experiment. tRIBO-seq distinguishes between ribosome-associated tRNAs and total tRNAs using nanopore sequencing, thus revealing their potentially distinct abundance, modification and fragmentation patterns in various conditions.

n1305839bdea3: Genetic variation can alter organ structure and function. n7b62038e9401: Providing dry solid contacts with on-demand macroscale frictional behaviour remains a formidable challenge in tribology, haptics and robotics. n3e3d624f582b: Far-from-equilibrium mixtures of active and passive molecules self-organize, but the principles remain unclear. n7bb46a69966a: A strong potential gradient can localize individual particles in a crystal or optical lattice by making ordinary hopping energetically costly. We track their individual quantum walks and characterize their strongly interacting scattering dynamics. Our study provides a bottom-up investigation of a Hamiltonian with kinetic constraints and offers an approach to exploring low-energy phases of fractonic matter. Strong potential gradients can localize individual particles, but interactions can still generate collective motion. n2c9c4009e46d: The candidate topological superconductor UTe2 exhibits a complex phase diagram with multiple superconducting states, and the nature of their coexistence is not yet resolved. nc6f97e83e90f: Despite decades of investigation, the fundamental molecular and cellular principles that enable bacteria to thrive within the tumor microenvironment have yet to be defined. n25d2c88ba945: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) affect up to 40% of patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, yet identification requires laborious, inconsistent manual chart review. n023325cfd732: Extending the depth reach of multiphoton microscopy for imaging neuronal population activity in the scattering mammalian brain is an ‘exponentially hard’ problem. n75eeaa4d85d6: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells induce target-cell death by producing effector proteases called granzymes. n78f449e6bf5c: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a fatal neurodegenerative disease increasingly linked to T cell responses, although the mechanisms driving T cell activation and disease progression remain unclear. n4e0fe1899bef: Many planetary systems survive the metamorphosis of their host stars into white dwarfs, as demonstrated by the detection of dusty circumstellar discs around these stellar remnants and chemical signatures of planetary debris in atmospheres of these stars. We propose that this structure results from the presence of two distinct planetary bodies within these discs, ranging in size from a few kilometres to the size of Pluto. n901edc1d018f: Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. n38ac05f045de: Embryonic hematopoiesis is thought to occur exclusively in the extraembryonic yolk sac before hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) arise in the aorta–gonad–mesonephros region. nda9387404a8b: Dysfunctional immune responses impair remyelination and contribute to neurodegeneration. While immune and metabolic responses to acute myelin injury are well characterized, myeloid cell adaptations to chronic myelin damage remain poorly understood. Here we performed a comparative analysis of genetic and toxic mouse models of acute and chronic demyelination, which identified a distinct microglial state associated with chronic demyelination, characterized by sustained pro-inflammatory activation, lysosomal lipid sequestration and reduced lipid droplet formation. Transcriptomics profiling further revealed a metabolic program marked by upregulated cholesterol synthesis and diminished sterol efflux. Treatment with a desmosterol mimetic possessing 24-dehydrocholesterol reductase inhibitor activity reversed this microglial state, attenuated pro-inflammatory signaling (including C-C Motif Chemokine Ligand 4 expression), reduced myelin damage and improved motor performance in a mouse model of leukodystrophy. Our findings uncover a pro-inflammatory microglial state characterized by lysosomal dysfunction and increased myelin reactivity, highlighting a novel therapeutic target for chronic demyelinating disorders.

n04b38b8fc204: In patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) treated with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, factors associated with efficacy overlap with prognostic biomarkers. The relationship between naive-like T cells and efficacy was independent of tumor microenvironment characteristics (assessed in 112 patients). In multivariate models, the naive-like phenotype outperformed clinicopathologic features such as inflammatory markers and tumor burden, remaining significant after adjusting for product expansion. An inverse correlation was observed between prior lines of therapy and the proportion of naive-like T cells in both product and matched apheresis samples, suggesting a benefit of earlier intervention. The key findings were validated in an independent cohort of 203 patients treated with axi-cel-based therapy or brexucabtagene autoleucel. Mass cytometry by time-of-flight analysis of products from a subgroup of 116 patients confirmed an association between a CD8 naive-like T cell phenotype lacking expression of exhaustion markers, such as TIGIT, LAG-3 and PD-1, and PFS. The evidence generated by this study has the potential to advance the development of more effective cellular therapies. A large comprehensive analysis of clinical trial samples from patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma who were treated with anti-CD19 CAR T therapy shows that a high proportion of naive-like and stem cell memory-like CCR7+CD45RA+ T cells in the pre-infusion CAR T product correlates with improved and prolonged clinical benefit, which was validated in an independent external cohort including different products.

n864b8b789cd7: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are present in biofluids and may be useful biomarkers to non-invasively monitor brain cells, but isolating cell type-specific EVs remains challenging. We first selected transmembrane proteins suitable as cell type-specific EV markers based on gene expression and EV proteomic data. We developed a high-purity EV isolation method and cataloged the proteins present on EVs in human cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. We then computationally identified cell type-specific candidate markers for isolating EVs from neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia. Using ultrasensitive immunoassays against several predicted neuron-specific proteins, we confirmed one marker, NRXN3, as present on EVs in cerebrospinal fluid and plasma. Finally, we developed efficient EV immuno-isolation methods and applied them to isolate NRXN3 + EVs. Our work provides a general methodology for the isolation of cell type-specific EVs, advancing the goal of using EVs to study brain diseases.

n5b8538ecaa59: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. n47dd3958d0c0: The breakdown of Hooke’s law marks the onset of nonlinear behaviour: when displacements become large, restoring forces weaken and Hookean proportionality fails. In quantum materials, intense optical excitation can drive the crystal lattice into a similar regime, where established linear relations between light, electrons and phonons no longer hold. Displacive excitation of coherent phonons, the principal mechanism for launching structural motion, typically assumes that lattice-driving forces scale linearly with the photo-excited carrier density. At high excitation, however, this linearity can break down, which fundamentally limits accessible lattice displacements. Here we show that such nonlinear limitations can be surpassed in a sliding ferroelectric by timing, rather than strengthening the optical drive. Time-resolved second-harmonic generation reveals that the interlayer-sliding phonon governing ferroelectricity saturates and even diminishes under single-pulse excitation. By means of first-principles calculations, we attribute this nonlinearity to band-specific electron–phonon coupling that induces competing forces on the lattice. By splitting the optical energy into two well-timed pulses that avoid populating counteracting states, we achieve markedly larger phonon amplitudes at fixed total fluence. The resulting enhanced sliding motion exposes a regime of anharmonic phonon coupling that emerges only far from equilibrium.

n5a8235cee095: Tools for manipulating RNA that rely on nonhuman proteins, such as ISC-based and Cas-based scaffolds, can lead to unintended and little-understood effects on human cells and present challenges in therapeutic translation. nd9e2b1652165: Chronic stress has lasting adverse consequences that can lead, over time, to depression, yet the optimal timeframe for effective therapies remains unclear. These neuronal adaptations mirrored both the progression of transcriptional changes and the emergence of depression-related behavioral phenotypes and were reversed by the antidepressant ketamine. nf4002d7207e2: In conventional, phonon-mediated superconductors, the transition temperature and the linear-in-temperature normal-state scattering rate are linked through the electron–phonon coupling strength. In cuprate high-temperature superconductors, no equivalent relationship between critical temperature and electron–boson coupling has been identified. Here we highlight such a link with electrons scattering off commensurate antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations of variable strength. We use d.c. resistivity and high-field magnetoresistance to extract the scattering rate in electron-doped La 2− x Ce x CuO 4 as a function of doping. We reveal a highly anisotropic inelastic component to the scattering rate whose magnitude diminishes markedly as doping increases. The correlation we highlight between the strength of scattering and the critical temperature then identifies low-energy spin fluctuations as the primary pairing glue in electron-doped cuprates. The contrasting magnetotransport behaviour in hole-doped cuprates suggests that the higher critical temperature in those materials cannot be attributed solely to an increase in the coupling strength to the antiferromagnetic fluctuations. The success in modelling La 2− x Ce x CuO 4 reinforces the notion that resolving the origin of high-temperature superconductivity in hole-doped cuprates may require more than a simple extension of the Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer theory.

n02df292caa0c: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P < 0.001), representing 15.5% of baseline weight; 83.1% achieved ≥10% and 22.4% achieved ≥20% weight loss, with consistent responses across age, baseline weight and socioeconomic strata. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up. nc8844cec566c: Strong coupling between two systems allows them to exchange coherent information before the systems decohere. This important regime in light–matter interactions has predominantly been reached in optical resonator configurations. Here we demonstrate strong coupling between optical and acoustic fields within a continuum of modes in a cavity-less configuration after a single pass through an optical waveguide. n2c7b769c5806: Thermodynamics establishes that information acquired through measurement can be converted into work, as exemplified by Maxwell’s demon and Szilard engines. Most experimental realizations of information engines, however, implicitly assume Markovian environments, in which information exchanged with the surroundings is irreversibly lost. Many physical systems instead exhibit environmental memory, with hidden degrees of freedom retaining correlations with the history of the system and giving rise to non-Markovian dynamics. Whether and how such concealed memory can be harnessed as a thermodynamic resource has remained an open question. Here we experimentally demonstrate the extraction of work from environmental memory. Using time-resolved measurements on an optically trapped Brownian particle in equilibrium, we implement a time-delayed double-measurement protocol that retrieves information through backflow from hidden bath degrees of freedom. We show that this information backflow alters the relaxation dynamics, can be quantified independently of initial state effects and—when appropriately exploited—enhances work extraction. Notably, we identify regimes in which the extracted work exceeds the energy stored in the observable degree of freedom alone. Our results establish environmental memory as an experimentally accessible thermodynamic resource and reveal how non-Markovian dynamics can be systematically explored to improve the performance of information engines operating in time-correlated environments.

n6ab0eab91600: Changes in oscillatory neural dynamics reflect—but may not necessarily determine—transitions between sleep stages and variations in sleep pressure. Here we show that sleep-control neurons innervating the dorsal fan-shaped body of Drosophila (dFBNs) produce slow-wave activity (SWA) that is causally linked to sleep. The dFBN ensemble contains bistable cells whose membrane voltages oscillate between hyperpolarized DOWN and depolarized UP states. The oscillations rely on interhemispheric competition of two half-centers connected by inhibitory glutamatergic synapses. dFBN-restricted interference with glutamate release disrupts SWA and baseline as well as rebound sleep, whereas the optogenetic replay of SWA induces sleep. dFBNs generate SWA throughout the sleep–wake cycle (despite mutual antagonism with arousing dopaminergic neurons) and adjust its power to sleep need via sleep history-dependent increases in excitability and homeostatic synaptic depression. The oscillatory format permits a continuous encoding of sleep pressure but requires mechanisms that convert the amplitude-modulated signal into binary sleep–wake states.

nab98ef4391a8: Silicon spin qubits offer a promising path to scalable quantum computing due to their compatibility with industrial semiconductor manufacturing. A key requirement for scaling quantum processors is the ability to perform high-fidelity operations in parallel across many qubits. However, simultaneous control remains a major challenge in silicon devices, as fidelities typically degrade under parallel operation. Here we identify microwave-drive-induced a.c.-Stark shifts as the dominant source of this degradation in a five-qubit silicon spin array. We address this by introducing a scalable mitigation protocol based solely on pairwise phase calibrations. Using tailored control pulses on a shared control line, we achieve primitive X and Y gate fidelities well above 99.99% for each qubit individually, with some approaching 99.999%. Furthermore, these fidelities are preserved above 99.99% during simultaneous operation of up to three qubits. During parallel five-qubit operation, fidelities remain above the widely targeted fault-tolerant threshold of 99.9%. By maintaining high-fidelity control during simultaneous operation, shared qubit-control lines can support the development of large-scale semiconductor quantum processors.
n538ada7aaa44: Planets are inherently three-dimensional objects shaped by their thermal structure and dynamics. Observations of transiting exoplanets have begun to uncover this three-dimensional nature, with JWST measuring their dayside atmosphere structure with eclipse mapping and exploring spectroscopic asymmetries in the limbs of planets during transit. Here we apply the novel transmission strings mapping method to the hot Jupiter WASP-17 b. With this method, we are not only able to extract hemispheric limb asymmetries from east-to-west, but can also map equator-to-pole variations around the transmitting atmosphere as a function of angle, spanning 0.6–12 μm. We find a clear transition in the thermal scale height around the limb of the atmosphere, with an approximately 650 K temperature difference between the morning ( $$85{8}_{-233}^{+434}\,{\mathrm{K}}$$ 85 8 − 233 + 434 K ) and evening $$1{,}52{2}_{-114}^{+116}\,{\mathrm{K}}$$ 1 , 52 2 − 114 + 116 K ). These results are consistent with both nightside emission and dayside eclipse mapping measurements, and represent a fully comprehensive set of observations for a transiting exoplanet. We are also able to constrain the abundances of H 2 O and CO 2 to constant values around the limb, providing observational constraints for results from global circulation models. The transmission string technique, combined with the outstanding observability of WASP-17 b, pushes the study of exoplanet atmospheres further into a three-dimensional understanding of hot Jupiter dynamics and chemistry.

n034f691828a2: Preterm birth is associated with breakdown of maternal–fetal tolerance and remains the leading cause of global mortality in young children. However, the role of self-reactive antibodies has been limited to a handful of pathogenic allo- and autoantibodies linked to pregnancy complications. Here we identify a shared autoreactive signature of pregnancy in pregnant sera (n = 2,719) relative to never-pregnant controls (n = 130), using proteome-wide autoantibody profiling. Across eight human pregnancy cohorts, we define autoreactivities associated with preterm birth by comparing preterm (n = 688) and term (n = 1,505) pregnancies. Within the signature, antibodies to IL1 receptor antagonist (IL1RA) induce resorption, inflammation and vascular malperfusion in pregnant mice. IL1RA localizes to placental endothelial adherens junctions, suggesting a role in vascular integrity. These findings identify a term pregnancy humoral immune program and shared changes preceding preterm delivery, including anti-IL1RA, which may have direct pathogenic consequences. Preterm labor is linked to breakdown of maternal–fetal tolerance. Rackaityte et al. report that some pregnant mothers harbor maternal autoantibodies, including those against IL-1 receptor antagonist, that may contribute to preterm delivery.

ne244b80c0746: The rapidly growing census of exoplanets now includes over a thousand multi-planet systems, revealing architectures that span more than four orders of magnitude in mass and five in orbital scale. Explaining the origin of this striking diversity remains a central challenge for planet formation theory, compounded by observational biases that limit access to Solar System-like regimes. Here we introduce architecture-agnostic metrics to uniformly analyse four independently defined samples of multi-planet systems, uncovering unifying patterns across their diversity. We identify a clear bimodality in system masses, dividing known architectures into two distinct families. The lower-mass family, predominantly hosted by subsolar-to-solar stars, exhibits tightly packed configurations with mass distributions consistent with the ‘peas-in-a-pod’ pattern and modal dynamical excitation comparable with that of the Solar System. By contrast, the high-mass family forms in metal-rich environments around solar-to-supersolar stars, displays gravitationally compact architectures and is an order of magnitude dynamically hotter than both the Solar System and the lower-mass counterparts. Their high level of dynamical excitation points to violent evolutionary pathways driven by global instabilities and planet–planet scattering. Together, these results show that the architectures of planetary systems are born from the combined influence of formation processes and host star properties. Signatures of these roots are preserved across the post-formation dynamical evolution that reshaped most known multi-planet systems.

n34f610d0cc6b: Using near-infrared photoswitchable photochromic genetically encoded probes, differential photoacoustic tomography (PAT) enables deep-tissue imaging with high resolution and sensitivity; however, current bacteriophytochrome-based probes are bulky multidomain proteins exceeding 55 kDa, which constrains their use for designing PAT molecular reporters. n4dd3906d7305: Programmable quantum devices provide a platform for controlling the coherent dynamics of quantum wave functions. Monitoring and feedback can control classically chaotic dynamics, but extending these approaches to quantum systems is challenging because chaotic evolution amplifies perturbations and is sensitive to noise and decoherence. Here we demonstrate adaptive monitored quantum circuits that incorporate conditional feedback into non-unitary evolution, using local mid-circuit measurements and resets to control quantum chaotic dynamics. We perform the experiments on an IBM superconducting quantum processor with up to 100 qubits, implementing a quantum version of the classically chaotic Bernoulli map. The map scrambles quantum information, whereas local measurements and feedback attempt to steer the dynamics towards a fixed point of the map. This competition drives a dynamical phase transition between quantum and classical dynamics, which we observe experimentally and describe theoretically using noisy simulations, matrix product states and mappings to statistical mechanics models. By successfully applying up to nearly 5,000 entangling gates and 5,000 non-unitary mid-circuit operations on systems up to 100 qubits, the quantum processor yields accurate estimates of the universal critical properties. Controlling quantum chaos requires using measurement and feedback that survive noise and decoherence. Such control is now achieved in a superconducting quantum processor and reveals a critical transition between quantum and classical dynamics.

n8578cfe7cc73: The Sun continuously releases a stream of charged particles known as the solar wind, threaded by magnetic field lines that occasionally fold back on themselves in sharp reversals called magnetic switchbacks. These structures are frequently observed by spacecraft near the Sun, but their formation mechanism remains an open question. Using measurements from Solar Orbiter at 0.55 AU, we report heavy ion observations within a magnetic switchback that provide direct evidence of its solar source. Elevated charge-state ratios of oxygen and carbon, combined with a depletion of helium relative to protons, indicate that the switchback plasma originated from hot, closed coronal loop structures. A semi-empirical coronal model, constrained by electron temperature and density measurements from the Solar Dynamics Observatory, traces the ion signatures to either a coronal hole boundary or loops within the coronal hole, implicating the source mechanism as interchange reconnection, where closed loops reconnect with open magnetic field and eject plasma. The proton velocity and magnetic field fluctuations of the switchback are in accordance with an outward-propagating Alfvén wave. These findings suggest that interchange reconnection and wave or turbulence mechanisms jointly govern switchback origin and propagation, respectively. Most importantly, we show that switchbacks preserve measurable signatures, carrying information about the physical processes that heat the solar atmosphere and accelerate the solar wind.

n29fbfd611b18: Picosecond current pulses can propagate with zero resistance far above the conventionally defined critical current values in type-II superconductors. n37c02bf0e6b1: Excitons—bound states of electrons and holes—can spontaneously condense into a quantum coherent ground state. 1 T -TiSe 2 , a layered transition metal dichalcogenide, is a candidate for realizing this phase in a bulk material, but its putative excitonic condensation is accompanied by charge-density-wave formation that obscures signatures of excitonic instability and fluctuations in this structural transition. Here we clarify the mechanism of exciton condensation in quasi-low-dimensional systems by tracking exciton dissociation as a function of photoexcitation fluence and temperature using few-femtosecond broadband extreme-ultraviolet absorption spectroscopy. We find that short-range excitonic fluctuations emerge before long-range-order formation in the ground state. We also observe enhanced excitonic susceptibility, identified by faster exciton dissociation near the phase transition temperature, consistent with excitonic instability in this material. These results provide a framework for understanding other excitonic insulator candidates proposed in quasi-one- or quasi-two-dimensional crystals.
